hu.name: Beecraigs Country Park

ro.name: Linlithgow Loch

ro.name: Piața The Cross
ro.text: Centrul istoric al orașului, marcat de o fântână ornamentală din secolul al XIX-lea, un loc plin de istorie.

ro.name: Canalul Union
ro.text: O cale navigabilă istorică ce traversează orașul, utilizată astăzi pentru agrement și plimbări pe mal.

ro.name: Castelul Blackness
ro.text: O fortăreață pe malul estuarului Forth, cunoscută sub numele de nava care nu a navigat niciodată.

ro.name: Parcul Beecraigs
ro.text: Un parc natural vast situat pe dealurile din apropiere, oferind trasee montane și o fermă de cerbi.

en.name: Linlithgow Palace
en.text: The magnificent 15th-century ruins of the royal residence and birthplace of Mary, Queen of Scots.

en.name: St Michael's Parish Church
en.text: A fine example of Scottish Gothic architecture, notable for its controversial 1960s aluminum crown spire.

en.name: Linlithgow Loch
en.text: A beautiful natural lake and Site of Special Scientific Interest located immediately north of the palace ruins.

en.name: The Cross and Wellhouse
en.text: The town's historic marketplace featuring an elaborate Victorian fountain designed to replicate a medieval original.

en.name: Union Canal
en.text: An engineered waterway completed in 1822 that passes through the town, now a popular leisure corridor.

en.name: Linlithgow Canal Centre
en.text: Based at the canal basin, this museum offers boat trips and explores the town's industrial canal history.

en.name: West Lothian County Buildings
en.text: An impressive Victorian civic building that serves as a reminder of Linlithgow's status as a county town.

en.name: Annet House Museum
en.text: A merchant's house from the 1780s that now houses a museum dedicated to the town's history and trades.

en.name: Blackness Castle
en.text: A 15th-century fortress on the Firth of Forth, often used as a film location for its ship-like shape.

en.name: Beecraigs Country Park
en.text: A large park in the Bathgate Hills providing a range of outdoor activities including a deer park and fishery.

descriptionAdvanced.de: Linlithgow liegt in den schottischen Lowlands zwischen Edinburgh und Stirling. Die Stadt ist weltbekannt für den Linlithgow Palace, der im 15. und 16. Jahrhundert eine bevorzugte Residenz der schottischen Monarchen war und heute als beeindruckende Ruine besichtigt werden kann. Neben der Palastanlage prägt der Linlithgow Loch das Stadtbild, ein natürlicher See, der als Vogelschutzgebiet dient. Historisch war die Stadt ein bedeutender Stopp auf dem Handelsweg zwischen den schottischen Machtzentren. Heute ist Linlithgow eine attraktive Pendlerstadt, die ihren historischen Charakter durch zahlreiche denkmalgeschützte Gebäude bewahrt hat. Die wirtschaftliche Basis hat sich von der Landwirtschaft und kleinen Industrien hin zu Dienstleistungen und Tourismus gewandelt, wobei der Charme der engen Gassen (bekannt als 'wynds') erhalten blieb.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: Linlithgow a skót alföldön, Edinburgh és Stirling között fekszik. A város világszerte ismert a Linlithgow-palotáról, amely a 15. és 16. században a skót uralkodók kedvelt rezidenciája volt, ma pedig lenyűgöző romként látogatható. A palota mellett a város arculatát meghatározza a Linlithgow Loch, egy természetes tó, amely madárvédelmi területként is szolgál. Történelmileg a város fontos állomás volt a skót hatalmi központok közötti kereskedelmi útvonalon. Ma Linlithgow egy vonzó ingázóváros, amely számos műemlék épületén keresztül megőrizte történelmi jellegét. A gazdasági bázis a mezőgazdaságról és a kisiparról a szolgáltatások és az idegenforgalom felé tolódott el, miközben a szűk sikátorok ('wynds') megőrizték régi bájukat.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Linlithgow este situat în zonele joase ale Scoției, între Edinburgh și Stirling. Orașul este cunoscut pe plan mondial pentru Palatul Linlithgow, care a fost o reședință preferată a monarhilor scoțieni în secolele XV și XVI și care astăzi poate fi vizitat ca o ruină impresionantă. Pe lângă palat, imaginea orașului este definită de Linlithgow Loch, un lac natural care servește drept rezervație pentru păsări. Din punct de vedere istoric, orașul a fost un punct de oprire important pe ruta comercială dintre centrele de putere scoțiene. Astăzi, Linlithgow este un oraș rezidențial atractiv, care și-a păstrat caracterul istoric prin numeroase clădiri protejate. Baza economică s-a transformat de la agricultură și micii industriași spre servicii și turism, păstrând în același timp farmecul aleilor înguste cunoscute sub numele de 'wynds'.
descriptionAdvanced.en: Linlithgow is situated in the Scottish Lowlands between Edinburgh and Stirling. The town is world-famous for Linlithgow Palace, which was a preferred residence of Scottish monarchs in the 15th and 16th centuries and can be visited today as an impressive ruin. In addition to the palace, the town's landscape is defined by Linlithgow Loch, a natural lake serving as a bird sanctuary. Historically, the town was an important stop on the trading route between Scottish power centers. Today, Linlithgow is an attractive commuter town that has preserved its historic character through numerous listed buildings. The economic base has shifted from agriculture and small industries towards services and tourism, while the charm of the narrow alleys (known as 'wynds') has been retained.
